scope: Follow-up of the 200 incomplete profile claims

reviews.claimText: Mainly active during daylight in the canopy.
reviews.note: The behaviour account supports daytime canopy activity and social families. NParks confirms the specialised digestive stomach.

reviews.claimText: Lives in social groups and spends much of its time in trees. Its specialised stomach supports digestion of leafy food.
reviews.note: The behaviour account supports daytime canopy activity and social families. NParks confirms the specialised digestive stomach.

reviews.claimText: Small population size and fragmented forest make protection of habitat and connectivity important.
reviews.note: NParks describes a small restricted population and canopy connections, including rope bridges. Habitat protection is the stated conservation response.

reviews.claimText: Broad snout, armoured body and a muscular, flattened tail. Only the eyes and nostrils may show above the surface.
reviews.note: NParks confirms broad snout and compressed muscular tail; ADW confirms eyes and nostrils can remain exposed above water.

reviews.claimText: Glides between trees and shelters in cavities in tall trunks. It appears largely solitary, but detailed social studies are limited.
reviews.note: ADW describes gliding and apparently solitary behaviour with limited study. The Singapore paper documents a tree-cavity nest.

reviews.claimText: Usually brownish-grey with a darker face and tail, pale forehead marking and three dark lines along the back. Markings vary, so a quick glimpse is insufficient to identify an unfamiliar civet confidently.
reviews.note: Physical description confirms dark extremities, pale forehead strip, dorsal lines and variable markings.

reviews.claimText: A bulky grey-brown body, blunt bristled muzzle, paired front flippers and a fluked tail. It has no dorsal fin.
reviews.note: ADW describes brown-grey skin, bristled rounded muzzle, paired foreflippers, fluked tail and absence of a dorsal fin.

reviews.claimText: Gives birth to live young. The Singapore field sources reviewed here do not establish a local breeding season or typical litter size, so no exact reproductive timetable is claimed.
reviews.note: The zoo's species account confirms live birth. The local field paper does not establish the withheld Singapore breeding timetable.

reviews.claimText: An egg-laying snake. Do not disturb hidden snakes, egg sites or shelter; young snakes must also be left alone.
reviews.note: The taxon record explicitly lists egg-laying reproduction. Leaving snakes and eggs alone is conservative wildlife guidance.

reviews.claimText: Lays eggs; local nesting timing and clutch sizes have not been verified.
reviews.note: The taxon record explicitly lists egg-laying reproduction. No unverified local breeding measurements are added.

reviews.claimText: Lays eggs. Local nesting dates, clutch size and incubation periods are not asserted from unrelated captive accounts.
reviews.note: The species record confirms egg-laying reproduction without relying on captive accounts of related monitors.

reviews.claimText: Confirmed on Pulau Ubin in 2008 after a long gap in verified records. NParks still includes the species in its 2025 Ubin conservation work. Its limited Singapore distribution does not mean every suitable mainland forest contains it.
reviews.note: The rediscovery paper confirms the 2008 Ubin record. The 2025 NParks update names greater mousedeer in continuing habitat work.

reviews.claimText: NParks documents catchment-forest records from 2006 and 2007. These are historical observations, while RDB3 (2024) retains the species as nationally Critically Endangered; neither is a current population census.
reviews.note: NParks lists the 2006 and 2007 catchment records. RDB3 supplies the separate current national category, not a census.

reviews.claimText: Native populations are associated with the Central Nature Reserves. The national assessment is Endangered in RDB3; encounter locations and resting sites are not mapped here.
reviews.note: NParks confines native populations to the central reserves. RDB3 lists Endangered, replacing the older profile's national category.

reviews.claimText: A familiar migrant at Sungei Buloh and other wetlands, including pond and canal edges. NParks records it throughout the year, with higher numbers commonly between November and January.
reviews.note: The two NParks accounts confirm wetland occurrence, year-round records and the November–January peak. They do not promise sightings.

reviews.claimText: Builds nests and lays eggs, often in colonies with other waterbirds. Both parents contribute to care. These species-level notes do not claim a local breeding colony.
reviews.note: The breeding account documents colonial nests, eggs and care by both parents. It does not establish a Singapore colony.

reviews.claimText: Fish are important prey, alongside frogs, aquatic invertebrates and other small animals; diet varies with habitat and prey availability.
reviews.note: The feeding, breeding and conservation sections support the field. Regional findings are not presented as Singapore measurements.

reviews.claimText: Builds a platform of reeds or sticks in wetland vegetation; trees and thickets can also be used. Both parents incubate and feed the young. Regional breeding seasons and clutch sizes vary, so none is presented here as a Singapore norm.
reviews.note: The feeding, breeding and conservation sections support the field. Regional findings are not presented as Singapore measurements.

reviews.claimText: The Heron Specialist Group identifies wetland alteration and disturbance as pressures across its range. Retaining suitable vegetated feeding and nesting habitat is a relevant local priority; no current Singapore decline rate is asserted.
reviews.note: The feeding, breeding and conservation sections support the field. Regional findings are not presented as Singapore measurements.

reviews.claimText: NParks records it in forest reserves and Pulau Ubin and highlights it in woodland birdwatching at Kranji Marshes. Bird Society lists it as a common resident; frequency of observation does not remove its national Vulnerable status.
reviews.note: NParks records the named sites; Bird Society supplies resident frequency. The RDB3 Vulnerable category remains separate.

reviews.claimText: Common in gardens, parks and other built environments. Being well established is different from being native.
reviews.note: NParks confirms common urban occurrence; the Singapore introduction study distinguishes established occurrence from native origin.
